ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS
August 202 6
DOB ISSUES MONTHLY ENFORCEMENT BULLETIN
Report Highlights DOB Enforcement Outcomes from August 2026 to
Deter Bad Actors and Keep New Yorkers Safe
New York, NY – The New York City Department of Buildings released its enforcement
bulletin for August 2026, which provides highlights of the agency’s actions to sanction
and deter bad actors in the construction industry through the enforcement of safety laws
and codes of conduct. Today’s bulletin includes summaries of DOB-imposed
disciplinary actions, including penalties, license suspensions, and revocations.
The actions below represent a portion of DOB’s overall work to enforce the City’s
building codes and safety laws, in addition to the thousands of inspections conducted
and violations issued by the agency each month for illegal building and construction
conditions.
DOB completed several major enforcement actions in August, including:
 13 violations and $130,000 in penalties imposed for failure to safeguard
construction sites at 13 locations.
 10 violations and $188,250 in penalties, including daily penalties, imposed for
illegal alterations in 2 locations.
 5 violations and $31,000 in penalties, including daily penalties, imposed for illegal
transient use in 1 location.
 1 violation and $10,000 in penalties issued for failure to perform the duties of a
Construction Superintendent.
 2 stipulations executed agreeing to remove illegal storage and/or cease
commercial use at 5 locations.
August’s enforcement efforts also resulted in the removal of 11 illegally stored school
buses at one location.
Below are individual enforcement highlights for August 2026:
Construction and Design Professionals
 DOB’s Special Enforcement Team (SET) audited twelve professionally certified
applications submitted by Professional Engineer Scott Dyer and found major
code non-compliances, including filing Alteration Type 2 applications despite
proposing changes in use, egress, and/or occupancy, which require Alteration

Type 1 applications for a new or amended Certificate of Occupancy; proposing
plans that fail to provide fire divisions separating a nonresidential kitchen from
other occupancies; failing to provide required special inspection reports;
proposing plans for an eating and drinking establishment contrary to the Zoning
Resolution without proof of existing lawful use; and various other violations of
code and rules, including the Zoning Resolution, Building Code, and
Administrative Code. Based on the audits, SET offered a voluntary surrender of
Professional Certification and Directive 14 privileges, which the Professional
Engineer agreed to.
 Master Fire Suppression Piping Contractor Richard Levine was issued a warning
letter regarding failure to cooperate with an investigation being conducted by the
Licensing Investigations Unit.
Bronx
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on Schimenti Construction Co for violations
recorded at 1998 Bruckner Blvd. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
provide protection for property after approximately 100 feet of fence collapsed,
leaving construction site open to the public.
Brooklyn
 $25,000 in penalties imposed on OP Buildings Corp. for violations recorded at
823 Maple Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard a
new building site after observing a lack of overhead protection during concrete
pouring operations. Inspectors also issued violations for failure to perform the
duties of a Construction Superintendent, and failure to protect adjoining property.
 $16,250 in penalties imposed on Technico Construction for violations recorded at
6315 14th Ave. DOB inspector issued violations for failure to safeguard the work
site after a worker fell due to an outrigger platform that was installed contrary to
manufacturer’s specifications came loose. Additionally, inspectors issued
violations for a non-compliant sidewalk shed, lack of barricades to protect
pedestrians and vehicles, and failure to provide required work design drawings
upon inspector’s request.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on Haian Honest Renovation for violations
recorded at 151 Baltic Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
safeguard after inspectors observed the fire escape at the multiple dwelling
building obstructed by a rear deck.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on FRSS Group Crop. for violations recorded at
428 Vanderbilt Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard
after observing inadequate wood shoring at multiple locations during structural
work.

 Following enforcement by DOB’s padlock unit, the owners of 2002 52nd Street
discontinued the illegal use of their vacant lot in an R5 residence district after
removing 11 school buses that had been stored on the property. Corrected
conditions pictured below.
Manhattan
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on Pofi Construction Corp. for violations recorded
at 1787 Madison Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard
after a brick fell from a suspended scaffold and struck the windshield of a vehicle.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on The Chetrit Group for violations recorded at 250
W 43rd Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard the
stalled construction site after observing an unsecured construction fence.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on Amsterdam Harlem Construction for violations
recorded at 696 West 158th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
safeguard the public and property after finding the new building construction site
unsecured and accessible to the public.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on Pavarini McGovern for violations recorded at
655 5 Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard the
public after a six-inch metal shin fell during hoist dismantling operations and
struck a pedestrian, and inspectors observed inadequate safety netting in place.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on L&Z Consulting Corp. for violations recorded at
440 East 79th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard
after observing an 8’ x 8’ trench in a fully operational garage that was missing
protection for the public and tenants.
Queens

 $122,500 in penalties imposed on Sandeep Aggarwal for violations recorded at
104-51 118th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations with daily penalties for
illegal conversions after observing a class A two-family dwelling converted to a
seven-family dwelling by adding five Single Room Occupancies (SROs).
 $31,000 in penalties imposed on 35-16 Astoria Blvd Holdings LLC for violations
recorded at 35-16 Astoria Blvd. DOB inspectors issued violations with daily
penalties for illegal conversions after observing two units being occupied for
transient use. Additionally, inspectors issued violations for lack of required means
of egress on every floor, missing illuminated signage, and lack of required
automatic class J fire alarm system which is required for transient use.
 $16,250 in penalties imposed on Terra Developers LLC for violations recorded at
11-37 44th Drive. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard a work
site after a large window panel fell on a worker and inspectors found no tie backs
or other safety measures in place at the site.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on Alba Services Inc. for violations recorded at
164-02 Jamaica Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard
following a worker injury resulting from an accent ladder that was improperly
positioned and not properly secured.
 $10,000 in penalties imposed on Triboro Construction Ass Inc. for violations
recorded at 73-19 68th Ave. DOB inspectors issued violation for failure to
safeguard the public after observing the fence at the property open to the public.
 Following enforcement by DOB’s padlock unit, a stipulation agreement was
executed with the owners of 47-11 90th Street to cease the commercial vehicle
storage and dead storage of motor vehicles in an R6B residence district.
Violating conditions pictured below.

 Following enforcement by DOB’s padlock unit, a stipulation agreement was
executed with the 106-29 79 Street, 106-28, 106-30, & 106-32 80th Street to
cease commercial vehicle storage and use of contractor’s yard in four vacant
residential lots in an R4-1 residence district. Violating conditions pictured below.
 Following enforcement by DOB’s padlock unit, a stipulation agreement was
executed with the owners of 116-06 229th Street to cease commercial storage in
the rear yard of a 1-family home in an R2A residence district. Violating conditions
pictured below.
 Following direct outreach by DOB’s padlock unit, the owners of 67-26 Groton
Street discontinued the illegal use of junk storage in the front yard of their one-
family home in an R4B residence district. Corrected conditions pictured below.
